title: ASEAN is dropping the ball on Myanmar
gist: Myanmar junta leader Min Aung Hlaing has outmanoeuvred ASEAN through bilateral state visits and new US (secret Tokyo talks, Naypyidaw visit) and Chinese engagement, rendering the bloc's Five Point Consensus increasingly irrelevant. Marston expects Singapore to hold the status quo in 2027 but Thailand to push full normalisation as chair in 2028, and urges Canberra to prepare rather than react.

themes.theme: ASEAN losing control of the Myanmar file

insights.claim: Min Aung Hlaing has visited China, India, Russia, Thailand and Vietnam this year, effectively outmanoeuvring ASEAN, which did not recognise the junta's January elections and bars high-level Myanmar representatives from its summits.
insights.speaker: Hunter Marston
insights.so_what: Myanmar's diplomatic isolation is eroding bilaterally regardless of ASEAN's formal position.

insights.claim: Min Aung Hlaing has travelled to five of ASEAN's 11 members this year, with reports he may soon visit Indonesia and Brunei, making the bloc's consensus-based position potentially irrelevant.

insights.so_what: Watch Indonesia/Brunei visits as markers of further normalisation.

themes.theme: ASEAN chair sequence and Myanmar normalisation

insights.claim: Singapore, taking over the ASEAN chair from the Philippines next month, is likely to preserve the status quo for one more year and keep Myanmar from full participation.
insights.speaker: Hunter Marston
insights.so_what: Expect no formal change in Myanmar's ASEAN status during 2027.

insights.claim: When Thailand takes the ASEAN chairmanship in 2028, Bangkok is certain to advocate full normalisation of Myanmar's membership.

insights.so_what: 2028 is the likely inflection for Myanmar's regional reintegration — a timing marker for Myanmar-exposed trade and investment.

insights.claim: The US delegation to Naypyidaw was led by Assistant Secretary of State for Intelligence and Research Michael Vance, ostensibly to free detained American businessman Adam Castillo, which served as a convenient pretext for engagement the Trump administration had long mulled.
